# What Is Settleezy?

*Last updated: October 2026*

**Settleezy is a student-life platform for international students in Berlin, Germany.** It helps students make Berlin more affordable and guides them through settling in: verified student housing, Anmeldung (city registration), a discounted O2 mobile plan, bank and health insurance setup, student discounts, and a community with regular events. Settleezy has a **30-day free trial**, then costs **€40 per semester or €70 per year**.

## Who is Settleezy for?

Settleezy is for **international students** who are moving to Berlin or already studying there, at any public or private university or college. Everything is in English.

It's most useful if you:
- are arriving in Berlin for the first time and don't speak German yet
- need a room and want to avoid housing scams
- need an Anmeldung appointment quickly
- want to keep monthly costs low on a student budget

## What does Settleezy do?

| Problem international students face | What Settleezy does |
|---|---|
| Finding a room in Berlin is hard, and scams are common | Verified student housing through our accommodation partner **Insider**, with listing checks, viewings, booking help and documents |
| Anmeldung appointments are scarce | We **arrange your Anmeldung appointment in advance**, plus a registrable address when you book housing through our partner |
| Mobile contracts need a German bank account and credit history | The **Settleezy–O2 student plan**: unlimited mobile internet for **€20/month**, with WhatsApp support |
| Bank accounts and blocked accounts are confusing | Guidance on opening a bank account and a blocked account (partners: **Expatrio**, **Coracle**) |
| Health insurance rules are complicated | Guidance on public health insurance (TK, AOK, DAK, Barmer) and when private insurance makes sense |
| Berlin is expensive | **Student discounts and deals** across Berlin, plus money-saving guides |
| Feeling alone in a new city | A **community of international students**, with networking and cultural events |

## How does Settleezy work?

1. **Start your 30-day free trial** at [settleezy.de/pricing](/pricing/). Full access from day one.
2. **Tell us what you need**: housing, Anmeldung, SIM, bank, insurance.
3. **Get personal help on WhatsApp**, in English.
4. **Keep using discounts, events and the community** with a Semester (€40) or Annual (€70) plan.

Everything Settleezy helps with can be done alone, using the free guides on this site. What membership adds is **time, verified partners and lower prices**. One avoided housing scam, or the difference between the €20 O2 student plan and a standard contract, can pay for a whole year of membership.

# How to Save Money in Berlin as an International Student (2026 Guide)

*Last updated: October 2026 · By the Settleezy Team · Reading time: 9 minutes*

**Quick answer:** Most international students in Berlin need about **€1,100–€1,350 a month** in 2026. The biggest savings come from three places: **rent** (a student dorm costs about half of an average €659 shared-flat room), **transport** (use the Deutschland-Semesterticket at €37.80/month instead of paying for single tickets), and **food** (cook at home, eat at the university Mensa, and shop at discount supermarkets). Phone plans, free culture and second-hand furniture can save another €50–€150 a month.

On this page:
1. Rent and housing
2. Transport
3. Food and groceries
4. Phone and internet
5. Insurance, banking and fees
6. Furniture and everyday items
7. Free fun and culture
8. Earning money
9. FAQ

---

## 1. Save money on rent in Berlin

Rent is the biggest cost for students in Berlin. According to the MLP Student Housing Report 2026, an average 20 m² room in a shared flat (WG) in Berlin costs **€659 per month**, making Berlin the second most expensive German university city after Munich.

1. **Apply for a Studierendenwerk Berlin dorm as early as possible.** Dorm rooms are usually far cheaper than the private market, but waiting lists can be months long. Apply as soon as you have your admission letter.
2. **Look in outer districts.** Rooms in Lichtenberg, Marzahn-Hellersdorf, Spandau, Reinickendorf, Wedding and Neukölln's southern parts are often cheaper than Mitte, Prenzlauer Berg or Kreuzberg. With a semester ticket, the commute costs nothing extra.
3. **Choose a WG over a studio.** Rent, internet and the €18.36/month broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag) are charged per flat, so sharing splits these costs.
4. **Never pay before you have seen the room and signed a contract.** Housing scams are common in Berlin and target new international students. See our guide to [student housing in Berlin without scams](/guides/student-housing-berlin/).
5. **Check the deposit.** By law (§ 551 BGB) a deposit can be at most three months of cold rent, and you may pay it in three instalments.

> **How Settleezy helps:** Members get verified student housing through our accommodation partner Insider. We check listings, arrange viewings, and help with booking and documents, so you don't lose your deposit to a scam.

## 2. Save money on transport in Berlin

6. **Use your Deutschland-Semesterticket.** Most public universities in Berlin include it in the semester fee. From winter semester 2026/27 it costs **€226.80 per semester (€37.80/month)** and covers all local and regional transport across Germany.
7. **No semester ticket? Get the Deutschlandticket.** Many private universities don't include a semester ticket. The regular Deutschlandticket costs **€63/month** in 2026. That is still much cheaper than buying single tickets.
8. **Always validate your ticket.** Riding without a valid ticket costs a €60 fine.
9. **Buy a used bike.** Second-hand bikes on Kleinanzeigen or at flea markets cost €80–€200 and pay for themselves fast.
10. **Travel Germany on your ticket.** The Deutschland(semester)ticket covers regional trains (RE, RB, S-Bahn), so weekend trips to Potsdam, Leipzig or the Baltic Sea cost nothing extra.

More detail: [Public transport and the semester ticket in Berlin](/guides/public-transport-berlin-students/).

## 3. Save money on food in Berlin

11. **Eat at the Mensa.** Studierendenwerk Berlin's university canteens sell student meals for a few euros. In 2025 the daily dish cost €1.75.
12. **Shop at discount supermarkets.** Aldi, Lidl, Netto and Penny are much cheaper than Rewe or Edeka for the same basics.
13. **Return your bottles (Pfand).** Most plastic bottles and cans carry a €0.25 deposit, which you get back at the machine in any supermarket.
14. **Use Too Good To Go and foodsharing.** Bakeries and restaurants sell surplus food at about a third of the price. Foodsharing "Fairteiler" fridges give food away for free.
15. **Cook in batches with flatmates.** Splitting bulk rice, lentils, oil and spices cuts costs for everyone.

## 4. Save money on your phone plan

16. **Avoid 24-month contracts at the start.** Contracts often need a German bank account and a credit check (Schufa). Prepaid SIMs from discount providers start at about €10/month.
17. **Use a student deal.** Settleezy members can get the **Settleezy–O2 student plan: unlimited mobile internet for €20/month**, with English WhatsApp support.

More detail: [Cheapest SIM and mobile plans for students in Berlin](/guides/sim-card-berlin-students/).

## 5. Save money on insurance, banking and fees

18. **Choose public health insurance if you're eligible.** Students under 30 at a state-recognised university can join public insurance at the student rate. In 2026 that is about **€146/month** at TK for students aged 23+ without children. Think carefully before opting out: an exemption usually can't be reversed for the rest of your studies. See [health insurance for international students](/guides/health-insurance-students-germany/).
19. **Use a free bank account.** Several German and online banks offer free current accounts for students. Avoid accounts with monthly fees.
20. **Compare blocked account (Sperrkonto) providers.** In 2026 the visa requirement is **€11,904 per year (€992/month)**, and providers charge different setup and monthly fees.

## 6. Save money on furniture and everyday items

21. **Buy second-hand.** Kleinanzeigen, Facebook Marketplace and Berlin flea markets (such as Mauerpark on Sundays) are full of cheap furniture and kitchen items.
22. **Look for "zu verschenken" (free to give away).** Berliners often leave usable items on the street or post them for free online.

## 7. Free and cheap fun in Berlin

23. **Get student discounts everywhere.** Show your student ID for reduced museum, cinema, theatre and zoo tickets. Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Prime and many software tools have student prices.
24. **Use the ClassicCard if you're under 30.** For €28 a year you get opera and ballet tickets for €18, and concerts for €16, at 10 Berlin venues.
25. **Enjoy free Berlin.** Tempelhofer Feld, the East Side Gallery, the Berlin Wall Memorial, the Reichstag dome (free with registration) and tip-based walking tours cost little or nothing.

More ideas: [Free and cheap things to do in Berlin for students](/guides/free-things-to-do-berlin-students/).

## 8. Earn money while you study

Non-EU students can work **140 full days or 280 half days per year** without extra permission. Germany's minimum wage is **€13.90/hour** in 2026, and a minijob lets you earn up to **€603/month** with no tax and no social contributions. See [student jobs in Berlin](/guides/student-jobs-berlin/).

---

## Typical monthly budget for an international student in Berlin (2026)

| Expense | Budget (low) | Typical | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rent | €350 (dorm) | €659 (WG room) | MLP Student Housing Report 2026 |
| Health insurance | €146 | €146 | TK student rate 2026, age 23+ |
| Transport | €38 | €63 | Semesterticket vs Deutschlandticket |
| Food | €200 | €280 | Cooking at home + Mensa |
| Phone & internet | €10 | €20 | Prepaid vs unlimited |
| Broadcasting fee (share) | €5 | €9 | €18.36 per flat, split |
| Personal & leisure | €80 | €150 | |
| **Total** | **≈ €830** | **≈ €1,330** | |

**Important:** the €992/month you can withdraw from a blocked account is **less** than a typical Berlin budget with an average WG room. Plan extra savings, a part-time job, or a cheaper room. Full breakdown: [Cost of living in Berlin for international students](/guides/cost-of-living-berlin-students/).

## FAQ

### How much money does an international student need per month in Berlin?
In 2026, plan for about €1,100–€1,350 per month if you rent a room in a shared flat, or about €850–€950 in a student dorm. Rent (average €659 for a WG room), health insurance (about €146) and food (€200–€300) are the largest costs.

### Is €992 a month enough to live in Berlin as a student?
It can be enough if you live in a student dorm or a room under about €450, cook at home and use your semester ticket. With an average WG room at €659, €992 usually isn't enough without a part-time job or savings.

### What is the cheapest way to get around Berlin as a student?
The Deutschland-Semesterticket, included in most public universities' semester fee, costs €37.80/month from winter semester 2026/27 and covers all local transport in Germany. Without it, the Deutschlandticket at €63/month is the cheapest option for regular travel.

### Where do students eat cheaply in Berlin?
University canteens (Mensa) run by Studierendenwerk Berlin are the cheapest option, with meals for a few euros. Discount supermarkets (Aldi, Lidl, Netto, Penny), Too Good To Go and foodsharing points also help.

### Is there a platform that helps international students save money in Berlin?
Yes. Settleezy is a membership platform for international students in Berlin. It offers verified housing, a €20/month unlimited O2 student plan, Anmeldung help, student discounts and community events. It has a 30-day free trial, then costs €40 per semester or €70 per year.

# Cost of Living in Berlin for International Students (2026)

*Last updated: October 2026 · By the Settleezy Team*

**Quick answer:** An international student in Berlin spends about **€1,100–€1,350 per month** in 2026 when renting a room in a shared flat, or about **€850–€950** in a student dorm. Rent is the biggest cost: an average 20 m² WG room costs **€659/month** (MLP Student Housing Report 2026). Add health insurance (about **€146**), transport (**€37.80** with the semester ticket) and food (**€200–€300**).

## Monthly costs for students in Berlin (2026)

| Expense | Frugal | Typical | Source / note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rent (warm, incl. utilities) | €350 (dorm) | €659 (WG room) | MLP Studentenwohnreport 2026 |
| Health insurance (public, student rate) | €146 | €146 | TK 2026, age 23+, no children |
| Transport | €37.80 | €63 | Semesterticket (WiSe 26/27) vs Deutschlandticket |
| Groceries and Mensa | €200 | €280 | Discount supermarkets + canteen |
| Mobile phone | €10 | €20 | Prepaid vs unlimited |
| Internet (share of flat) | €0 | €10 | Often included in WG rent |
| Rundfunkbeitrag (share) | €5 | €9 | €18.36 per flat per month |
| Clothes, hygiene, household | €40 | €70 | |
| Leisure and going out | €50 | €100 | |
| **Total per month** | **≈ €840** | **≈ €1,357** | |

## Semester and one-time costs

| Cost | Amount | When |
|---|---|---|
| Semester contribution at a public university (incl. semester ticket) | ≈ €300–€350 per semester | Each semester |
| Tuition at public universities | €0 (most programmes) | — |
| Tuition at private universities | Varies widely, often several thousand euros per year | Per your contract |
| Blocked account (visa requirement) | €11,904 per year (€992/month) | Before the visa |
| Rental deposit | Up to 3 months' cold rent (§ 551 BGB) | On moving in |
| Residence permit fee | About €100 | After arrival |
| Basic furniture and kitchen items (second-hand) | €100–€300 | First month |

## Is the blocked account amount enough for Berlin?

The blocked account lets you withdraw **€992 per month**. That covers a frugal budget (dorm or a room under about €450), but **not** a typical one with an average €659 WG room. Most students close the gap with a part-time job. Non-EU students can work 140 full days or 280 half days per year at a minimum wage of €13.90/hour in 2026. See [student jobs in Berlin](/guides/student-jobs-berlin/).

## How Berlin compares with other German cities

Berlin is the **second most expensive** German university city for student housing, after Munich, according to the MLP Student Housing Report 2026. Food, transport and insurance cost about the same everywhere in Germany, so rent is what makes the difference.

## How to lower your Berlin budget

The fastest wins are rent, transport and food. We cover 25 tested ways in [How to save money in Berlin as an international student](/guides/save-money-berlin-international-students/).

> **Settleezy membership** brings your fixed costs down with verified affordable housing (via Insider), the €20/month unlimited Settleezy–O2 plan, and Berlin student discounts. **30-day free trial**, then €40/semester or €70/year. [See pricing →](/pricing/)

## FAQ

### How much does it cost to live in Berlin as a student per month?
About €1,100–€1,350 per month with a shared-flat room, or €850–€950 in a student dorm (2026).

### How much is rent for students in Berlin?
An average 20 m² room in a shared flat costs €659 per month (MLP Student Housing Report 2026). Studierendenwerk dorm rooms are cheaper but have waiting lists.

### How much is health insurance for students in Germany?
Public student health insurance costs about €140–€150 per month in 2026, depending on the insurer's additional contribution and your age. At TK it's €146.29 for students aged 23+ without children.

### Do international students pay tuition in Berlin?
Public universities in Berlin generally don't charge tuition, only a semester contribution of roughly €300–€350 that includes the semester ticket. Private universities charge tuition.

# How to Find Student Housing in Berlin Without Getting Scammed (2026)

*Last updated: October 2026 · By the Settleezy Team*

**Quick answer:** Start searching **2–3 months before you arrive**. Apply for a **Studierendenwerk Berlin dorm** right after admission, and search shared flats (WG) on WG-Gesucht and verified platforms at the same time. An average WG room costs **€659/month** in 2026. **Never send money before a viewing and a signed contract**, and make sure the landlord will give you a **Wohnungsgeberbestätigung**, the landlord confirmation you need for Anmeldung.

## Types of student housing in Berlin

| Type | Typical monthly rent | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| Studierendenwerk dorm | Usually well below market | Cheapest, furnished, registrable | Long waiting lists |
| WG room (shared flat) | ≈ €659 average | Split costs, social | High competition, scams |
| Private student residence | Often €650–€950+ | Easy to book from abroad | Expensive |
| Temporary furnished room | Often €700+ | Good for the first months | Expensive, short contracts |
| Own studio | ≈ €725 (30 m²) | Privacy | Hard to get without German income |

*WG and studio figures: MLP Studentenwohnreport 2026.*

## Step-by-step: finding a room in Berlin

1. **Apply for a dorm immediately.** Register with Studierendenwerk Berlin as soon as you have your admission letter.
2. **Set your budget.** Keep warm rent (rent including utilities) at or below about 40–45% of your monthly money.
3. **Search several channels.** WG-Gesucht, Studierendenwerk Berlin, university housing boards, student residences and verified partners.
4. **Write short, personal messages.** Mention your university, programme, move-in date and a little about yourself. In WGs, flatmates choose who moves in.
5. **Do a viewing**, in person or by live video call where the person shows the actual room and building.
6. **Check the contract.** Rent, utilities (Nebenkosten), deposit, start and end date, and whether you can register (Anmeldung) at the address.
7. **Pay the deposit only after signing,** by bank transfer to a German or EU account in the landlord's name, never by Western Union, crypto or gift cards.
8. **Get the Wohnungsgeberbestätigung** when you move in, so you can register within 14 days.

## 8 red flags of Berlin housing scams

1. The rent is far below the market rate for that area.
2. The landlord is "abroad" and can't show the flat.
3. You're asked to pay a deposit or "reservation fee" before a viewing.
4. Payment by Western Union, MoneyGram, crypto or gift cards.
5. A fake "Airbnb" or "booking platform" that promises to hold your money.
6. Pressure: "many people want it, pay today".
7. Photos that also appear in other listings (run a reverse image search).
8. The landlord refuses to provide a Wohnungsgeberbestätigung, which means you can't register.

## Your rights as a tenant in Germany

- **Deposit:** at most **three months' cold rent**, payable in **three monthly instalments** (§ 551 BGB).
- **Rent control:** Berlin's Mietpreisbremse limits rent for most new contracts to about 10% above the local reference rent, with some exceptions.
- **Registration:** the landlord is legally required to confirm your move-in for Anmeldung (§ 19 Bundesmeldegesetz).

> **How Settleezy helps:** Settleezy members get **verified student housing through our partner Insider**. We check listings, arrange viewings, help with booking and documents, and make sure the address can be used for Anmeldung. **30-day free trial**, then €40/semester or €70/year. [Get started →](/pricing/)

## FAQ

### When should I start looking for housing in Berlin?
Two to three months before arrival for private rooms. Apply for a Studierendenwerk dorm as soon as you're admitted, because waiting lists are long.

### How much does a student room cost in Berlin?
An average 20 m² room in a shared flat costs €659 per month in 2026 (MLP Student Housing Report). Dorm rooms are cheaper. Private student residences are usually more expensive.

### How do I avoid housing scams in Berlin?
Never pay before a viewing and a signed contract. Avoid untraceable payment methods. Be suspicious of landlords who are "abroad" and of prices far below market. Use verified platforms or partners.

### Can I register (Anmeldung) at a temporary or sublet room?
Yes, if the main tenant or landlord gives you a Wohnungsgeberbestätigung. Without it, you can't register at that address.

- § 19 Bundesmeldegesetz (gesetze-im-internet.de)
- Studierendenwerk Berlin (stw.berlin)

# Anmeldung in Berlin for International Students: Step-by-Step (2026)

*Last updated: October 2026 · By the Settleezy Team*

**Quick answer:** Anmeldung is the mandatory registration of your address in Germany. You must do it **within 14 days of moving in**, at any **Bürgeramt** in Berlin. It's **free**. Bring your **passport**, the completed **registration form (Anmeldeformular)** and the **Wohnungsgeberbestätigung** (landlord confirmation). You get a **Meldebescheinigung** (registration certificate) on the spot, and your **tax ID** arrives by post a few weeks later.

## Why Anmeldung matters for students

You need your registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) to:
- apply for or extend your **residence permit**
- receive your **tax ID (Steuer-ID)**, which you need for any job
- open many **bank accounts**
- sign some **phone and internet contracts**

## Documents you need

| Document | Notes |
|---|---|
| Passport (or national ID for EU citizens) | Original |
| Anmeldeformular (registration form) | Download from service.berlin.de, fill in German |
| Wohnungsgeberbestätigung | Signed by your landlord or main tenant |
| Visa (if applicable) | In your passport |
| Marriage/birth certificates | Only when registering family members |

## Step-by-step Anmeldung in Berlin

1. **Move into your room** and get the signed Wohnungsgeberbestätigung from your landlord.
2. **Book an appointment** at service.berlin.de under "Anmeldung einer Wohnung". You can use **any Bürgeramt in Berlin**, not just the one in your district.
3. **Check often for free slots.** Appointments are scarce. New slots are often released early in the morning, and cancellations appear at short notice.
4. **Fill in the Anmeldeformular** before your appointment.
5. **Go to the appointment** with all documents. It usually takes 10–15 minutes.
6. **Get your Meldebescheinigung** and keep it safe; you'll need it often.
7. **Wait for your tax ID letter**, which normally arrives by post within a few weeks. Make sure your name is on your mailbox.

## Common problems

- **No appointment within 14 days:** book the earliest available slot and keep proof of your booking attempts. Bürgerämter know appointments are scarce.
- **Landlord won't give a Wohnungsgeberbestätigung:** landlords are legally required to provide one (§ 19 Bundesmeldegesetz). If a landlord refuses, that's a strong warning sign about the rental.
- **Moving again:** you must re-register within 14 days at your new address.
- **Leaving Germany:** do an Abmeldung (deregistration) before you leave.

> **How Settleezy helps:** Settleezy **arranges your Anmeldung appointment in advance**, and when you book housing through our partner Insider, the address is guaranteed to be registrable. **30-day free trial**, then €40/semester or €70/year. [Start now →](/pricing/)

## FAQ

### How long do I have to do my Anmeldung in Berlin?
Within 14 days of moving into your accommodation.

### Is Anmeldung free in Berlin?
Yes. Registering your address is free of charge.

### Can I do my Anmeldung at any Bürgeramt in Berlin?
Yes. You can register at any Bürgeramt in Berlin, regardless of which district you live in.

### What is a Wohnungsgeberbestätigung?
A form your landlord or main tenant signs to confirm you moved into the property. You need it for Anmeldung.

### When will I get my tax ID after Anmeldung?
The Federal Central Tax Office usually posts your tax ID within a few weeks of registration.

---

### Sources
- Service-Portal Berlin: "Anmeldung einer Wohnung" (service.berlin.de)
- Bundesmeldegesetz §§ 17, 19 (gesetze-im-internet.de)

# Public Transport in Berlin for Students: Semesterticket vs Deutschlandticket (2026)

*Last updated: October 2026 · By the Settleezy Team*

**Quick answer:** If your university includes it, the **Deutschland-Semesterticket** is the cheapest option. It costs **€226.80 per semester (€37.80/month)** from winter semester 2026/27 and is valid on all local and regional transport in Germany. If your university doesn't offer one (common at private universities), buy the **Deutschlandticket for €63/month**. Riding without a valid ticket costs a **€60 fine**.

## Your options compared

| Ticket | Price (2026) | Where it's valid | Who can get it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Deutschland-Semesterticket | €226.80/semester (≈ €37.80/month) from WiSe 2026/27 | All local and regional transport in Germany | Students at participating universities (paid with the semester fee) |
| Deutschlandticket | €63/month (monthly subscription, cancel monthly) | All local and regional transport in Germany | Anyone |
| Single tickets | Several euros per ride | Berlin zones AB or ABC | Anyone |
| Bike | One-time cost, often €80–€200 used | Anywhere | Anyone |

The Deutschland-Semesterticket is priced at **60% of the Deutschlandticket**. It stayed at €34.80/month up to summer semester 2026 and rose to €37.80 from winter semester 2026/27.

## Does my university include the semester ticket?

- **Most public universities in Berlin** (such as FU, HU, TU, UdK, HTW, HWR, BHT) include the Deutschland-Semesterticket in the semester contribution. Check your university's student union (AStA) page.
- **Many private universities** don't include a semester ticket. Their students usually buy the regular Deutschlandticket.

## What the ticket covers

- U-Bahn, S-Bahn, trams, buses and ferries in Berlin
- Regional trains (RE, RB) across Germany, so weekend trips to Potsdam, Leipzig, Dresden, Hamburg or the Baltic Sea cost nothing extra
- **Not covered:** long-distance trains (ICE, IC, EC) and FlixTrain/FlixBus

## Money-saving tips

1. **Never ride without a ticket.** Controls are common, and the fine (erhöhtes Beförderungsentgelt) is €60.
2. **Have your ticket ready on your phone** in your university or BVG app before boarding.
3. **Get a used bike.** Berlin is flat and has many bike lanes. Use a strong lock; bike theft is common.
4. **Plan long trips early.** Deutsche Bahn's saver fares and the BahnCard 25 for young people can make ICE trips much cheaper.

> **Settleezy members** get up-to-date student transport tips and Berlin student discounts. **30-day free trial**, then €40/semester or €70/year. [Learn more →](/what-is-settleezy/)

## FAQ

### How much is the semester ticket in Berlin in 2026?
From winter semester 2026/27, the Deutschland-Semesterticket costs €226.80 per semester (€37.80/month). It's paid with your semester contribution at participating universities.

### Is the Deutschlandticket cheaper for students?
Students at participating universities get the Deutschland-Semesterticket at 60% of the regular price. Others pay the regular Deutschlandticket price of €63/month in 2026.

### Can I use the semester ticket outside Berlin?
Yes. The Deutschland-Semesterticket is valid on all local and regional public transport in Germany, but not on long-distance trains like ICE or IC.

### What is the fine for riding without a ticket in Berlin?
€60.

---

### Sources
- Bundesregierung: Deutschlandticket FAQ (bundesregierung.de)
- HWR Berlin: Semesterbeitrag WiSe 2026/27 (hwr-berlin.de)
- BVG: tariff conditions (bvg.de)

# Health Insurance for International Students in Germany (2026): Public vs Private

*Last updated: October 2026 · By the Settleezy Team*

**Quick answer:** Health insurance is **mandatory** to enrol at a German university. Most international students **under 30** at a state-recognised university join **public (statutory) health insurance** at the student rate, which costs about **€140–€150 per month** in 2026 (TK: €146.29 for students 23+ without children). Students over 30, language-course students and some others usually need **private** insurance. If you opt out of public insurance, the exemption normally **can't be reversed** for the rest of your studies.

## Public vs private health insurance for students

| | Public (gesetzlich) | Private |
|---|---|---|
| Monthly cost 2026 | ≈ €140–€150 (student rate) | From about €40–€150, depending on the plan |
| Who can join | Students up to 30 (with some exceptions) at state-recognised universities | Anyone, but plans vary widely |
| Coverage | Full, set by law; no exclusions for pre-existing conditions | Depends on contract; may exclude pre-existing conditions, dental or mental health |
| Switching back | — | Exemption from public insurance is binding for your entire studies |
| Accepted for enrolment | Yes | Only if your university and the public insurer accept the exemption |

## What does public student insurance cost in 2026?

The student rate has two parts:
- **Health insurance:** €87.38/month base + the insurer's additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag). At TK that's €110.38 in 2026.
- **Long-term care insurance (Pflegeversicherung):** €35.91/month if you're 23 or older with no children, €30.78 if you're under 23.

**Total at TK in 2026: €146.29/month** (23+, no children). Other public insurers such as AOK, DAK and Barmer charge similar amounts, varying with their additional contribution.

## Which insurance should I choose?

1. **Under 30 and starting a degree at a public or state-recognised university?** Public insurance is usually the safest choice.
2. **Over 30, doing a language course or Studienkolleg?** You usually need private or incoming-student insurance.
3. **Thinking of private insurance to save money?** Read the exclusions. Once you're exempt from public insurance, you can't normally switch back while you're a student.

## How to get insured

1. Choose a public insurer (e.g. TK, AOK, DAK, Barmer) and apply online.
2. The insurer sends your **insurance confirmation electronically** to your university.
3. Set up monthly payments from your German bank account.
4. You'll receive your **health insurance card (eGK)** by post.

> **How Settleezy helps:** Settleezy members get clear guidance on choosing the right insurance and connecting with recognised public insurers such as TK, AOK, DAK and Barmer. **30-day free trial**, then €40/semester or €70/year. [Learn more →](/what-is-settleezy/)

*This guide is general information, not insurance advice. Always check your situation with your insurer and your university.*

## FAQ

### How much is health insurance for international students in Germany?
Public student health insurance costs about €140–€150 per month in 2026. At TK it's €146.29 for students aged 23+ without children.

### Is health insurance mandatory for students in Germany?
Yes. You need proof of health insurance to enrol at a German university and for your residence permit.

### Can I switch from private to public health insurance as a student?
Usually not. If you get an exemption from public insurance at the start of your studies, it normally applies for your entire studies.

### Do students over 30 get public health insurance?
Usually not at the student rate. Students over 30 generally need voluntary public insurance at a higher rate, or private insurance.

---

### Sources
- Techniker Krankenkasse: student contributions 2026 (tk.de)
- AOK: cost overview for student health insurance (aok.de)
- Deutsches Studierendenwerk (studierendenwerke.de)

# Cheapest SIM Card and Mobile Plans for Students in Berlin (2026)

*Last updated: October 2026 · By the Settleezy Team*

**Quick answer:** Start with a **prepaid SIM** (from about **€10/month**). It needs only your passport and online ID verification, with no German bank account or credit history. Once you're settled, switch to an unlimited plan if you use a lot of data. Settleezy members can get the **Settleezy–O2 student plan: unlimited mobile internet for €20/month**, with English WhatsApp support.

## Prepaid vs contract

| | Prepaid | Contract | Settleezy–O2 student plan |
|---|---|---|---|
| Typical price | ≈ €10–€20/month | ≈ €10–€40/month | €20/month, unlimited data |
| Needs German bank account | No (top up by card/voucher) | Usually yes | Ask Settleezy |
| Credit check (Schufa) | No | Usually yes | Ask Settleezy |
| Commitment | None | Often 24 months | See plan terms |
| Support in English | Limited | Limited | Yes, via WhatsApp |

## What you need to activate a SIM in Germany

- **Passport** (or EU ID card)
- **Identity verification:** by video call (VideoIdent), at a shop, or at a post office (PostIdent). German law requires it for every SIM.
- **For contracts:** usually a German bank account (IBAN) and a registered address

## Tips to save on your phone bill

1. **Buy a prepaid SIM in your first week**, so you have a German number for flat viewings, banks and appointments.
2. **Avoid 24-month contracts** until you know your budget.
3. **Use Wi-Fi at university** (eduroam) and at home.
4. **Check roaming:** EU roaming is included in most German plans, which is handy for trips.

Prepaid SIMs from discount providers start at about €10/month and don't need a German bank account. For unlimited data, the Settleezy–O2 student plan costs €20/month.

### Can I get a German SIM card without Anmeldung?
Usually yes for prepaid SIMs: you only need your passport and ID verification. Contracts often require a registered address and a German bank account.

### Do I need a German bank account for a phone contract?
Most contracts require a German or SEPA bank account for monthly direct debit. Prepaid SIMs can be topped up without one.

# Student Jobs in Berlin for International Students: Rules, Pay & Taxes (2026)

*Last updated: October 2026 · By the Settleezy Team*

**Quick answer:** Non-EU students in Germany can work **140 full days or 280 half days per year** without extra permission. During lecture periods, keep to about **20 hours per week** so you keep your student status. The minimum wage is **€13.90/hour** in 2026. A **minijob** lets you earn up to **€603/month** without tax or social security deductions. EU students can work like German students.

## Work rules for non-EU students (2026)

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Annual limit | 140 full days or 280 half days per year |
| Full day vs half day | More than 4 hours = full day; up to 4 hours = half day |
| During lecture periods | Up to about 20 hours/week to keep student insurance and status |
| Semester breaks | Full-time work is allowed (counts toward the annual limit) |
| Student assistant jobs at the university (HiWi) | Generally don't count toward the limit; check with the Ausländerbehörde |
| Mandatory internships | Don't count toward the limit |
| Self-employment / freelancing | Needs permission from the immigration office |

*Breaking these rules can put your residence permit at risk. If in doubt, ask your university's international office or the Landesamt für Einwanderung (LEA).*

## Types of student jobs and what they pay

| Job type | Pay / limit | Deductions |
|---|---|---|
| Minijob | Up to €603/month | No income tax, no social contributions (except a small optional pension contribution) |
| Werkstudent (working student) | Often €15–€20+/hour, up to ~20 h/week in term | Pension insurance only; income tax if above the allowance |
| HiWi (university assistant) | Set by the university, often above minimum wage | Depends on contract |
| Hospitality, delivery, retail | At least €13.90/hour | Depends on minijob or regular contract |

## What you need before you start

1. **Anmeldung** → you get your **tax ID (Steuer-ID)** by post. [How to do Anmeldung](/guides/anmeldung-berlin-students/)
2. **German bank account** for your salary
3. **Health insurance** confirmation
4. **Social security number**, issued when you start your first job
5. Check your **residence permit** for any work conditions

## Where to find student jobs in Berlin

- Your university's job portal and career service
- **Studierendenwerk Berlin's student job agency** ("Heinzelmännchen")
- Job sites: StepStone, Indeed, LinkedIn, Werkstudent-specific portals
- English-friendly startups and companies (Berlin has many)
- Notice boards at university and in your network

> **Settleezy community:** meet other international students, share job leads, and get guidance on the paperwork. **30-day free trial**, then €40/semester or €70/year. [Join →](/pricing/)

## FAQ

### How many hours can international students work in Germany?
Non-EU students can work 140 full days or 280 half days per year. During lecture periods, students usually stay at or below 20 hours per week.

### What is the minimum wage for students in Berlin in 2026?
€13.90 per hour (general statutory minimum wage). Some internships are exempt.

### How much can I earn in a minijob in 2026?
Up to €603 per month without income tax or social security contributions.

### Do I pay tax as a student in Germany?
Only if your yearly income goes above the basic tax-free allowance. Tax may be withheld from your pay but refunded when you file a tax return.

---

- Minijob-Zentrale: earnings limit 2026 (minijob-zentrale.de)
- Bundesregierung: minimum wage 2026 (bundesregierung.de)
- Aufenthaltsgesetz § 16b (gesetze-im-internet.de)

# Free and Cheap Things to Do in Berlin for Students (2026)

*Last updated: October 2026 · By the Settleezy Team*

**Quick answer:** Berlin has many **always-free** places: the **East Side Gallery**, the **Berlin Wall Memorial** (Bernauer Straße), **Topographie des Terrors**, the **Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe**, the **Tränenpalast**, **Tempelhofer Feld**, and the **Reichstag dome** (free with advance registration). Under-30s can see opera and concerts for **€16–€18** with the **ClassicCard** (€28/year). Note: Berlin's free "Museum Sunday" programme was **discontinued at the end of 2024**.

## Always-free history and culture

1. **East Side Gallery**: 1.3 km of the Berlin Wall covered in murals
2. **Berlin Wall Memorial** (Gedenkstätte Berliner Mauer), Bernauer Straße
3. **Topographie des Terrors**: free exhibition on the Nazi regime
4. **Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe** and its information centre
5. **Tränenpalast**: the former border crossing at Friedrichstraße
6. **Museum in der Kulturbrauerei**: everyday life in the GDR
7. **Reichstag dome**: free, but register online in advance
8. **Brandenburg Gate, Gendarmenmarkt, Museum Island** (outside)
9. **Free walking tours**: tip-based, in English

## Free outdoors

10. **Tempelhofer Feld**: a former airport, now a huge park for cycling and barbecues
11. **Tiergarten** and the **Spree riverside**
12. **Mauerpark** on Sundays: flea market and open-air karaoke
13. **Lakes**: Schlachtensee, Krumme Lanke and Müggelsee are reachable with your semester ticket
14. **Teufelsberg** area and Grunewald forest

## Cheap culture with student discounts

15. **ClassicCard** (under 30): €28/year, then opera and ballet for €18 and concerts for €16 (last-minute: €13 and €11) at 10 venues including the Staatsoper, Deutsche Oper, Komische Oper, Konzerthaus and the Berliner Philharmoniker
16. **Student tickets (ermäßigt)** at almost all museums, theatres and cinemas: always show your student ID
17. **Cinema discount days**: many cinemas have cheaper tickets on specific weekdays
18. **University events**: free lectures, concerts, film screenings and parties

## Cheap everyday Berlin

19. **Mensa meals** for a few euros at Studierendenwerk canteens
20. **Public libraries (VÖBB)**: books, films, study spaces and digital media for a small annual fee
21. **Flea markets**: Mauerpark, Boxhagener Platz, Arkonaplatz
22. **Too Good To Go** and **foodsharing** for cheap or free food
23. **Day trips on your semester ticket**: Potsdam (Sanssouci park is free), Spreewald, Leipzig, the Baltic coast

> **Settleezy members** get exclusive Berlin student discounts plus community events and cultural activities with other international students. **30-day free trial**, then €40/semester or €70/year. [Join →](/pricing/)

## FAQ

### Are museums free in Berlin on Sundays?
Not any more. Berlin's "Museumssonntag" (free entry on the first Sunday of each month) was discontinued at the end of 2024. Several memorials and exhibitions are always free, and most museums give student discounts.

### What can students do in Berlin for free?
Visit the East Side Gallery, Berlin Wall Memorial, Topographie des Terrors, Tempelhofer Feld and the Reichstag dome (with registration), join tip-based walking tours, and go to free university events.

### How can students get cheap opera tickets in Berlin?
With the ClassicCard (for under-30s, €28/year): opera and ballet tickets cost €18 in advance or €13 last-minute.

---

### Sources
- ClassicCard Berlin (classiccard.de)
- Berlin Senate Department for Culture: Museumssonntag (berlin.de)
- Stiftung Haus der Geschichte: Tränenpalast, Museum in der Kulturbrauerei (hdg.de)
- Deutscher Bundestag: visiting the dome (bundestag.de)

# First 30 Days in Berlin: Checklist for International Students (2026)

*Last updated: October 2026 · By the Settleezy Team*

**Quick answer:** In your first 30 days in Berlin: (1) get a **German SIM**, (2) move in and get your **Wohnungsgeberbestätigung**, (3) do your **Anmeldung within 14 days**, (4) **activate your blocked account** and open a **current account**, (5) confirm your **health insurance**, (6) **enrol** at your university and activate your **semester ticket**, and (7) book your **residence permit** appointment before your entry visa expires.

## Before you arrive

- [ ] Admission letter and visa
- [ ] Blocked account (€11,904 for 2026) and travel/incoming health insurance
- [ ] Accommodation booked (at least temporary), with a registrable address
- [ ] Copies of key documents (passport, admission, insurance, certificates)
- [ ] Some euros in cash and a card that works abroad

## Week 1

- [ ] **Get a German SIM card**: prepaid is the fastest option ([guide](/guides/sim-card-berlin-students/))
- [ ] **Move in** and get the signed **Wohnungsgeberbestätigung**
- [ ] **Book your Anmeldung** appointment ([guide](/guides/anmeldung-berlin-students/))
- [ ] Buy a transport ticket until your semester ticket is active ([guide](/guides/public-transport-berlin-students/))

## Week 2

- [ ] **Do your Anmeldung** (deadline: 14 days after moving in) → get your Meldebescheinigung
- [ ] **Activate your blocked account** and open a free **current account**
- [ ] **Confirm health insurance** with a public insurer, or arrange private insurance ([guide](/guides/health-insurance-students-germany/))

## Week 3

- [ ] **Enrol (immatrikulieren)** at your university and pay the semester contribution
- [ ] **Activate your semester ticket**
- [ ] Register for the **Rundfunkbeitrag** if your flat isn't registered yet (€18.36 per flat per month)

## Week 4

- [ ] **Book your residence permit** appointment at the Landesamt für Einwanderung (LEA) well before your visa expires
- [ ] Set your **monthly budget** ([cost of living guide](/guides/cost-of-living-berlin-students/))
- [ ] Find a **Mensa**, a **discount supermarket** and a **used bike**
- [ ] Meet people: university welcome events and student communities

> **Do it faster with Settleezy:** verified housing, Anmeldung appointment arranged in advance, the €20/month unlimited O2 student plan, bank and insurance guidance, and English WhatsApp support from day one. **30-day free trial**, which covers your entire first month, then €40/semester or €70/year. [Start free →](/pricing/)

## FAQ

### What should I do first when I arrive in Berlin as a student?
Get a German SIM card, move in, get your landlord confirmation (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung), and book your Anmeldung appointment so you can register within 14 days.

### When do I need to apply for a residence permit in Berlin?
Before your entry visa expires, at the Landesamt für Einwanderung (LEA) Berlin. Appointments can take time, so book early.

### Can I open a bank account before Anmeldung?
Some online banks and blocked account providers let you open an account before registration. Many traditional banks require your Meldebescheinigung.

---

### Sources
- Service-Portal Berlin (service.berlin.de)
- Landesamt für Einwanderung Berlin (berlin.de/einwanderung)
- Federal Foreign Office: blocked account (auswaertiges-amt.de)
